ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There are four identical light bulbs, where bulbs $L_1$ and $L_2$ are connected in series with the primary coil of an ideal transformer, and bulbs $L_3$ and $L_4$ are connected in parallel across the secondary coil. All four bulbs are glowing normally.

1. Find the turns ratio $n_1$: $n_2$ of the transformer's primary and secondary coils.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There are four identical light bulbs, where bulbs L1 and L2 are connected in series with the primary coil of an ideal transformer, and bulbs L3 and L4 are connected in parallel across the secondary coil. All four bulbs are glowing normally. 1. Find the turns ratio n1:n2 of the transformer's primary and secondary coils.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the primary coil of the transformer, labeled n1; in the left-side circuit, bulb L1 is located on the upper branch, and bulb L2 is located on the lower branch; they are in the same series circuit as the primary coil. On the right side of the figure is the secondary coil, labeled n2; bulbs L3 and L4 are respectively connected on two branches between the two ends of the secondary coil, so L3 and L4 are connected in parallel across the two ends of the secondary coil. Reasoning: Let the current when one bulb emits light normally be I. Because the four bulbs are completely identical and all emit light normally, the normal operating current of each bulb is the same. L1 and L2 are in series with the primary coil, and the current in a series circuit is the same, so the primary-coil current I1 = I. L3 and L4 are connected in parallel across the two ends of the secondary coil, and each emits light normally, so the current in each branch is I, and the total current of the secondary coil I2 = I + I = 2I. An ideal transformer satisfies that the current ratio is inversely proportional to the turns ratio: I1/I2 = n2/n1. Substituting gives I/(2I)=n2/n1, so n2/n1=1/2, that is, n1:n2=2:1.
